newsitem.title: USA: HSN Inc to buy stake in Ticketmaster. [CORRECTED 12:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: HSN Inc to buy stake in Ticketmaster. [CORRECTED 12:50 GMT]

text.p: HSN Inc said on Tuesday (corrects from Monday) it planned to acquire a 47.5 percent stake in Ticketmaster Group Inc from Microsoft Corp co-founder Paul Allen in a stock-for-stock transaction.
(Corrects company name throughout, to HSN Inc from Home Shopping Network Inc.)

Under the terms, HSN Inc will issue about 7.2 million shares to Allen in exchange for about 12.3 million shares of Ticketmaster. The shares to be issued by HSN represent about 11 percent of its equity.
The transaction is expected to close in July, it said.
HSN said it also intended to acquire additional shares on the open market in order to increase its ownership in Ticketmaster to more than 50 percent.

Under the deal, up to 3.3 million additional shares of HSN also will be issued in August 1998 if the average closing price of its stock falls below $29 per share for the first 20 consecutive trading days in July 1998. The adjustment is to be made to ensure that Allen will receive value for his stock equal to but not to exceed $209 million, it said.
The two companies' operating results are to be consolidated for accounting purposes, but they will continue to operate as independent entities, it said.
After the initial exchange of shares is closed, Allen and other Ticketmaster executives will join HSN's board of directors.

"This transaction creates a powerful partnership between two leaders in electronic commerce and provides Ticketmaster with additional channels for growth," Ticketmaster President and Chief Executive Frederic Rosen said in a statement.
